exampleSetups.label: K'ril Tsutsaroth: Ranged
exampleSetups.notes:
The scorching bow's special attack is highly recommended as using it on K'ril Tsutsaroth allows players to avoid most damage, extending trip length, along with the bow also providing the highest Ranged DPS.

Inventory:

- A mage switch and rune pouch with runes to cast Blood barrage, if using the Ancient Spellbook.
- A toxic blowpipe for special attacks (with no Scorching bow)
- 3-4 Armadyl brew, Bastion potions or Ranging potions
- 9-10 Super restores or Prayer potions
- 1 Extended anti-venom+ or Antidote++(4)
- Guthan's equipment for healing (teams only)
- A Construction cape or house tab for escaping
- Some food: Marlins, Manta rays or Saradomin brews
- A Zamorak item if not equipped
- Ghommal's hilt 1 or better for teleporting there
- Explorer's ring 4 (For high alchemy)

exampleSetups.label: K'ril Tsutsaroth: Solo Melee
exampleSetups.notes:
The player focuses on Magic defence while using Protect from Melee to defend themselves against K'ril's powerful melee attacks. This will leave them vulnerable to his prayer smash attack however, so they should keep their health high to avoid being comboed out by the resulting damage from this attack and from minions.

Inventory:

- 2-3 Super combat potions
- 7-8 Super restores or Sanfew serums
- 1 Antidote++ (If using Super Restores and not using a Serpentine helm)
- 14 Anglerfish
- Rune pouch with runes to cast Blood Barrage for healing
- A Construction cape or house tab for escaping
- A saturated or imbued heart to boost the player's Magic level to increase their Magic defence (Optional)
- Explorer's ring 4 (For high alch if not bringing runes)

exampleSetups.label: K'ril Tsutsaroth: Melee Tank
exampleSetups.notes:
By focusing on melee defence, players can use Protect from Magic to protect themselves from K'ril's magical attacks and his prayer smash. However, his melee attacks are significantly more accurate compared to his magic attack and have a higher max hit. K'ril's melee attack is slash-based, so high slash defence is recommended. Because of this it is not recommended to use this setup without Justiciar armour. The given inventory setup assumes a team of 3 players

Inventory:

- Special attack weapon (if not Arclight)
- 3-4 Super combat potions
- 7-8 Super restores or Sanfew serums
- 1 Extended anti-venom+ or Antidote++
- 4-5 Saradomin brews
- Rune pouch with runes to cast Vengeance or Potion share
- Guthan's equipment for healing
- A Construction cape or house tab for escaping
- Some food: Marlin, Manta rays, Sharks or Saradomin brews
- Explorer's ring 4 (For high alch if not bringing runes)

exampleSetups.label: K'ril Tsutsaroth: Melee
exampleSetups.notes:
As a melee attacker, you should maximise your damage per second while keeping your ranged and melee defences high. Fortunately melee gear has high ranged and melee defences, hence you can simply use your max DPS gear. It might be worthwhile to bring an extra antidote++ for the tank should they run out, as they have quite limited inventory space.

Inventory:

- Special attack weapon (if not Arclight)
- 4-5 Super combat potions
- 9-10 Super restores or Prayer potions
- Rune pouch with runes to cast Potion share
- 1 Extended anti-venom+ or Antidote++(4)
- Guthan's equipment for healing
- A Construction cape or house tab for escaping
- Some food: Marlin, Manta rays, Sharks or Saradomin brews
- Explorer's ring 4 (For high alch if not bringing runes)

exampleSetups.label: K'ril Tsutsaroth: Magic
exampleSetups.notes:
Tumeken's shadow provides the highest DPS against K'ril. Mage is not recommended with any weapon weaker than a Tumeken's shadow. Using the 5:0 method to avoid all damage from K'ril is highly recommended due to magic armour's low defences, while praying Protect from Range to protect against the range minion. Blood Barrage is used to heal off the melee and range minions in between kills.

A Purging staff can be used, but requires the player to bring a way to heal themselves between kills, such as Sanguinesti staff.

Inventory:

- Staff to autocast Ancient magicks against the minions like Eldritch Nightmare staff, Kodai wand, or Blood ancient sceptre
- Saturated heart to boost magic level
- Sanfew serums, or Super restores and Antidote++
- Extended stamina potions or Stamina potions (it is unlikely that you will need any run energy restoration if you have a high enough agility level)
- Anglerfish or other high healing food (the better you get at performing the 5:0 method, the less food you will need to bring)
- Rune pouch with runes to cast Blood Barrage for healing and Ice Barrage to freeze Tstanon Karlak
- A Construction cape or house tab for escaping
- Explorer's ring 4 (for high alch and energy recharges)

strategy: Greater demons can be assigned by Krystilia, Chaeldar, Konar, Nieve/Steve, and Duradel/Kuradal. Despite their "greater" status, they possess a somewhat lackluster drop table, with their two most valuable drops being the rune full helm and the hard clue scroll. There are many different types of greater demons residing around Gielinor; however, with the exception of the Wilderness Slayer Cave, all have the same drop table.

When not killing greater demons as part of Konar or Krystilia's tasks, players have many spots to choose from. The most common spots are the Chasm of Fire and Catacombs of Kourend. The Chasm of Fire is a cannonable area in a small space, allowing for plenty of AFK and fast kill times, along with contracts for challenging a stronger version of Yama. Catering to the increased drop rates will require more banking and less AFK time, however. The Catacombs of Kourend has access to the ancient shard and dark totem piece drops. It is also a Multicombat area, allowing for players to AFK until the aggression timer expires, which can be easily reset.

In the Wilderness, players have several spots to kill greater demons from. The most common would be the Wilderness Slayer Cave due to the enhanced drops, multiway area and allowing a cannon, but this spot is frequented often by player killers, so players should not bring items they are not willing to lose. The Demonic Ruins is a much worse spot, due to being a far deeper multiway area and players tend to teleport in via Annakarl Teleports. A more secluded spot is the Lava Maze Dungeon, but accessing it requires a long trek around the maze, or 82 Agility (boostable at 77) for a shortcut that cuts a significant amount of time.

exampleSetups.label: Melee
exampleSetups.notes:
Melee is one of the best ways to kill green dragons at any levels, and becomes the most effective way in terms of kills per hour and cost when using a dragon hunter lance. Setups can vary depending on the player's equipment, stats and how much the player is willing to risk in case of a death. With dragon hunter lance, high stats and the Wilderness elite diary completed (for noted bones) the player can kill up to 300-330 dragons per hour.

Equipment:

Viggora's chainmace offers the highest damage output, but due to the cost of using revenant ether it is best to use the dragon hunter lance for better profit per hour. Proselyte armour is recommended for its prayer bonus if using damage-boosting prayers such as Piety. Otherwise, the player should wear cheap defensive armour (such as dragonhide or rune armour) for extra defence against the dragons and player killers. Dragonfire shield is strongly recommended for its strength bonus and good defensive stats.

Inventory:

- 2-dose divine super combat potion or 1-dose super combat potion
- 1-dose extended antifire or 2-dose antifire potion
- 2-3 prayer potions
- Burning amulet
- Looting bag
- A teleport for banking and restoring stats such as a ring of dueling or a teleport to house tablet
- Some food such as cooked karambwan or monkfish
- Herb sack (optional)
- Soul bearer (optional)

exampleSetups.label: Ranged
exampleSetups.notes:
The Webweaver bow, Craw's bow, and toxic blowpipe offer slightly higher kills per hour than using a dragon hunter lance, but due to the high cost of using these weapons it is only recommended for Ironmen who wish to bank dragon bones for Prayer experience. Otherwise, melee usually offers higher kills and better profit per hour.

Equipment:

Void Knight equipment is the best option due to its damage-boosting set effect. If wearing full Void Knight equipment however, it is recommended to only use the spot west of Dark Warriors' Fortress between level 12 and 14 Wilderness, as you will not risk untradeable items on death. If wearing black d'hide, it is recommended to use the spot east of black salamanders in level 20-22 Wilderness as there are more green dragon spawns. If not wearing an anti-dragon shield, the player must use Protect from Magic or extended super antifire potions.

Inventory:

- 2-dose divine ranging potion or 1-dose ranging potion
- 2-dose antifire potion
- 1-dose super defence (optional)
- 2-4 prayer potions
- Burning amulet
- Looting bag
- A teleport for banking and restoring stats such as ring of dueling or teleport to house tablet
- Some food such as summer pie, karambwan, or monkfish
- Herb sack (optional)
- Soul bearer (optional)

strategy: Green dragons can be assigned as a slayer task at level 52 combat by Krystilia after partial completion of Dragon Slayer I. As Krystilia is the only Slayer master to assign green dragons, they must be fought in the Wilderness, and other variants outside the Wilderness do not count. They attack with melee and dragonfire, thus some protection against it should be considered. Due to their large size, they are usually able to be safespotted with ranged or halberd-like weapons. As dragons, they are also weak to dragonbane weapons.

A majority of dragons are above the level 20 line, thus a level 30 teleport such as an amulet of glory or royal seed pod is recommended for escaping player killers. A small cluster of three dragons can be found below level 20 Wilderness just west of the Dark Warriors' Fortress, making it ideal for killing with good attention, as the use of a teleport tab is enough to escape any hostile players. The dragons near the Lava Maze are above level 30 Wilderness, and thus it is not recommended to kill them there.
summary: A Krystilia-only Wilderness task (52 combat, partial Dragon Slayer I) so every kill must be in the Wilderness; Corsair Cove green dragons do not count. They melee and breathe dragonfire, so bring an anti-dragon or dragonfire shield and antifire, and since they are large they are usually safespotted with ranged or a halberd. The safest spot is the cluster of three dragons below level 20 just west of the Dark Warriors' Fortress where a teleport tab escapes any PKer; the wiki says most of the other dragons, including the largest group (11) east of the Bone Yard hunter area, are above the level 20 line, so carry a level 30 teleport such as a glory or royal seed pod.

exampleSetups.label: Equipment
exampleSetups.notes:
Players who are not safespotting gryphons are recommended to use melee equipment. A minimum of 30 kg is required for normal gryphons and 40 for the shellbane gryphon to avoid taking damage from their special attack.

They are best killed in the south-western multicombat room of the eastern task-only cave using a venator bow and a dwarf multicannon. 30 kg can be reached in a maxed range setup by using a black mask (i) rather than a slayer helmet (i), using a granite ring, or by substituting avernic treads (max) for echo boots. Bring a tortugan shield for the superior, and a cannon.

exampleSetups.label: Shellbane gryphon: Melee
exampleSetups.notes:
Since the Shellbane Gryphon's knockback is effective against players with less than 40 kg of worn equipment, some of the best options do not necessarily provide the highest damage, but rather a balance between strength bonus and heavy weight.

A 40kg+ setup can be easily achieved with most melee armour coupled with both a tortugan and dragonfire shield, even when using a slayer helmet. If a black mask is used, its higher weight over the slayer helmet means that the player can slot in an avernic defender for better DPS. If not being used, the dragonfire shield is recommended to meet this requirement.

If using low-level gear, adamant armour may be preferred to rune as it is heavier.

Inventory:

- Special attack weapon such as a dragon dagger. If using the Arkan blade as a main-hand damaging weapon, its special attack will suffice.
- Divine super combat potions / super combat potions; or super attack potions + super strength potions if those are not available.
- Means to teleport to house, such as Teleport to house (tablet) or Construction cape
- Rune pouch, with runes to cast Resurrection spells and a Book of the Dead.
- If A Kingdom Divided has not yet been completed, simply bring nature runes and fire runes for High Level Alchemy.
- Explorer's ring 4 if high alching runite item drops and using the Arceuus Spellbook.
- Herb sack if collecting herb drops.
- Bonecrusher or bonecrusher necklace for Prayer experience and to reduce number of items on ground.
- A bracelet of…

exampleSetups.label: Shellbane gryphon: Melee (POH)
exampleSetups.notes:
Due to Shellbane gryphon's cave's proximity to fairy ring, players who have ornate rejuvenation pool and fairy ring built in their player-owned house can teleport out between kills and restore their hitpoints, special attack, and prayer points. This has three major benefits:

- Less supplies used
- Allows special attacks to be used more often
- Allows player to bring better equipment
- The weight aspect of gryphon's knockback can be ignored, since it's unlikely that the gryphon will do that more than once per kill and the damage taken is only moderate.

~50-65 kills per hour can be achieved with this method, depending on what gear player has access to, and how attentively they are playing.

Inventory:

- Special attack weapon
- Tortugan shield
- Divine super combat potions / super combat potions
- Surge potions to get an extra spec every kill, the cooldown gets reset when you use your POH pool
- Means to teleport to house, such as Teleport to house (tablet) or Construction cape
- Rune pouch
- Book of the Dead if using thralls instead of Vengeance
- Explorer's ring 4 if high alching rune drops
- Bonecrusher for passive prayer experience

requiredItems: Equipment weighing at least 30 kg equipped (avoids the knockback special)
strategy: Gryphons can be assigned as a slayer task by Vannaka, Chaeldar and Mortimer after completion of the Troubled Tortugans quest. Additionally, both Nieve and Duradel may assign gryphons after the perk Wings Spread has been purchased.

Gryphons are found exclusively on The Great Conch. There are three lairs for gryphons; a western cavern, an eastern cavern (Slayer task only) and a lair in the centre of the island which leads to the Shellbane gryphon. Both the eastern and western caverns have a southern room that is multi-combat and cannon-able.

Gryphons attack with melee and have a special attack which causes knockback and moderate damage if the player's weight of their worn equipment is too low; this is 30 for normal gryphons and 40 for the boss. They are weakest to melee, ideally from stabbing attacks. While being a bit more resistant to magic, they have a 50% weakness to air spells.
summary: A 51 Slayer task on the Great Conch (Troubled Tortugans and 45 Sailing) from Vannaka, Chaeldar and Mortimer, or Nieve/Duradel after buying Wings Spread. Gryphons melee and have a knockback special that hurts if your equipped weight is under 30 kg, so wear heavy gear; they are weakest to stab melee and 50% weak to air spells. The best method is the south-western multicombat room of the eastern task-only cave with a cannon and a venator bow or melee; the western cave has a full safespot. A tortugan shield is only required for the dire gryphon superior and the Shellbane gryphon boss.

requiredItems: Lit bug lantern (must be lit and equipped; 33 Firemaking)
strategy: Harpie bug swarms are mid-level slayer monsters that require a Slayer level of 33 to kill. A lit bug lantern, which requires a Firemaking level of 33 to light, is required to damage these monsters (the lantern must be lit and equipped). If you do not have 33 Firemaking, you cannot be assigned harpie bug swarms as a Slayer task.

Harpie bug swarms should be an easy task for well-equipped mid-level players; their abundance as well as the fact that they remain aggressive to players until level 93 combat makes this task very click-easy. As harpie bug swarms are very accurate, and will often hit for up to 6 Hitpoints, it is advisable to have Defence levels from 40-50+ and to bring food appropriate for the player's level, such as lobsters. Another option is to keep Protect from Melee up and recharge prayer at the relatively nearby altars.
It is recommended to bring nature runes while slaying this monster since it has many drops that can be alched to free up inventory spaces, and fire runes are frequently dropped from this monster.
summary: A Vannaka-only task needing 33 Slayer and 33 Firemaking; you cannot damage them unless a lit bug lantern is equipped. They are aggressive up to combat 93 and very accurate for up to 6, so bring food or use Protect from Melee. The wiki now recommends the swarms east of the Colossal Wyrm Remains in Varlamore, which have safespots, no poisonous neighbours and a quetzal landing site next to a bank, over the classic Tai Bwo Wannai spot on Karamja where a cannon can be used but antipoison is needed.
usefulItems: Food or prayer for Protect from Melee

exampleSetups.label: Cerberus: Melee
exampleSetups.notes:
Inventory:

- 1-2 Divine super combat potions
- 6-9 Prayer potions or Super restores
- Special attack weapon (e.g. Elder maul or Dragon claws)
- Spectral spirit shield
- If you are using the Scythe of Vitur or Abyssal bludgeon, bring a one-handed weapon such as Arclight to use during the summoned souls attack while the spectral spirit shield is equipped
- Rune pouch with runes and Book of the Dead for casting resurrection spells on the Arceuus spellbook.
- Runes for Ward of Arceuus to reduce prayer drain; stacks with spectral spirit shield
- Death runes and soul runes for Death Charge to allow for more special attacks per trip. These inventory slots can be substituted for more food or prayer potions.
- Wrath runes for casting Demonic Offering, can be used to restore prayer once per kill in the middle of a ghost attack to save prayer potion doses. Not as helpful if using a spectral spirit shield.
- House tablets (or Construct. cape/Max cape) or Desert amulet 4
- Sharks or higher tier food for remaining inventory space
- Bluefin make a good alternative high-healing food, due to their extra prayer restore being useful at this boss with its high usage of prayer points.

- Notes

exampleSetups.label: Cerberus: Ranged
exampleSetups.notes:
As she possesses a Magic level of 220, the Twisted bow can be used on her with devastating effect. Cerberus does not move in to attack players with melee, meaning that players are only subjected to magic and ranged attacks outside of the triple attack mechanic. Ranging also allows players to quickly avoid the lava marker attack since it does not appear instantly when launched at a distance. The Bow of Faerdhinen is also effective, but slightly worse than the Toxic blowpipe if using rune darts or better. Crystal armour should be worn if using the Bow of Faerdhinen.

Inventory:

- Special attack weapon (e.g. Toxic blowpipe or Saradomin godsword)
- Spectral spirit shield and a one-handed weapon alongside it
- Book of the Dead for casting resurrection spells on the Arceuus spellbook.
- Rune pouch with runes for Resurrect Greater Skeleton or either of the other Thrall spells. It does not matter which style of thrall is used.
- Runes for Ward of Arceuus are optional, but recommended to reduce prayer drain; stacks with spectral spirit shield
- House tablets (or Construct. cape/Max cape) or Desert amulet 4
- 1 Divine bastion potion or 1 Divine ranging potion
- 6-9 Prayer potions or Super restores
- Sharks or higher tier food for remaining inventory space
- Bluefin make a good alternative high-healing food, due to their extra prayer restore being useful at this boss with its high usage of prayer points.

- Notes

strategy: Hellhounds can be assigned as a slayer task at 65 combat level by various Slayer masters. They can be found in a variety of locations around Gielinor. The task is very straightforward as regular hellhounds only attack with their fairly accurate melee bites; it is recommended to either safespot them or keep Protect from Melee on at all times. Hellhounds are primarily known for their high drop rate of hard clue scrolls, at a rate of 1/64, or 1/32 if killing in the Wilderness with a imbued ring of wealth. They also drop ensouled hellhound heads and the smouldering stone.

Outside of the Wilderness, hellhounds are primarily killed in the Stronghold Slayer Cave for general slayer, as there are four rooms of three or four hellhounds in each one, and a dwarf multicannon can be set up in their caves. They may also be killed in the Catacombs of Kourend for ancient shards and dark totem pieces. The catacombs do not allow for a cannon, but is a Multicombat area and allows for relative AFK training, especially with a Venator bow, and is also quite close to the entrance. Once the aggression timer expires, the player can simply run south and up the vine to the Giants' Den to reset aggression. Some players opt to restore prayer at an altar and teleport back to this location using Xeric's talisman's Xeric's Heart option or the Kourend Castle Teleport spell (requires 48 Magic and completion of Client of Kourend to unlock the spell).

In the Wilderness, hellhounds are primarily killed in the Wilderness Slayer Cave, with a group of five slightly stronger hellhounds in a multicombat area. The drop rate of the smouldering stone from these hellhounds is increased by 50%, and they have access to the Wilderness Slayer Cave drop table, which can help offset some supply costs. However, the cave itself is a very popular player killing hotspot despite the hellhounds being below level 20 Wilderness, and players killing them here should not bring any items they are unwilling to lose. These hellhounds are generally killed if assigned by Krystilia.
summary: A mid-to-high level task from Vannaka, Chaeldar, Konar, Nieve, Duradel and Krystilia. Hellhounds only bite with accurate melee, so either safespot them (they are 2x2 and get stuck on rocks) or keep Protect from Melee on; they are demons, so Arclight/Emberlight work well. The Stronghold Slayer Cave is the standard spot (four rooms, task-only, cannon allowed), the Catacombs of Kourend are multicombat for AFK venator bow or burst plus ancient shard and totem drops, and Wilderness tasks are done in the Wilderness Slayer Cave. Their draw is the 1/64 hard clue rate (1/32 with an imbued ring of wealth in the Wilderness).

trainingSummary.cons: Commonly assigned and long task. Using the cannon will result in a loss due to lack of drops. Killing Cerberus effectively requires expensive equipment, and the profit is very inconsistent due to the value mostly being in the rare unique drops.
trainingSummary.pros: Cerberus can be killed on task for good long-term profit. Relatively low-effort task if killing regular hellhounds, and good source of hard clue scrolls.
trainingSummary.recommendation: Block unless killing Cerberus for profit

strategy: Hydras can be assigned as a slayer task at level 95 Slayer. This is a task exclusive to both Konar quo Maten and Mortimer; the latter requires partial completion of Fallen From Grace.

Mortimer is the best way for players to obtain hydra tasks. Not only does Mortimer assign more on average, he also has various incentives when completing these tasks from him, such as additional kills, increased clue scrolls or superior drop rates. Given the nature of his assignments however, players should try to complete the task accordingly to benefit from the incentive. Mortimer has a small pool of tasks, and coupled with his unique ability for the player to assign themselves appropriately from two or three (after completing 50 tasks with him), means it is very easy to be given hydras from him. Assuming that every task can be offered with two of the normal tasks (which have a weight of 10) are blocked, there is a 4.0% chance for hydras to be offered.

Konar, the original master who could assign hydras, has a huge pool despite having a total lower weight of 250. To get the best possible chance to be given a hydra task, the player must block a lot of other tasks, especially ones that are the same, close to or higher than hers, such as metal dragons, drakes and wyrms (both of which share the same weight as hydra tasks). Because of the larger pool of tasks and traditional slayer assignments, it is harder to get a task from Konar compared to Mortimer, and the only incentive for completing the task from Konar are slayer points and the chance for brimstone keys.
summary: A 95 Slayer task from Konar and Mortimer, found only on the lower level of the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon. Hydras alternate ranged and magic in sets of one to three attacks and later spit poison pools, so start with the protection prayer for your weaker defence and swap when they switch; ranged (twisted bow) or a dragonbane weapon is standard because of their very high magic level. Wear boots of stone, brimstone or granite unless you have the Elite Kourend & Kebos Diary. The Alchemical Hydra boss can be killed instead while on task and is far more profitable.

strategy: Ice warriors are mid-level ice elementals. They have a 100% elemental weakness to fire spells. Ice warriors can be assigned by Krystilia for a Wilderness Slayer task, or by Vannaka or Mazchna for normal tasks.
Kamil fought during Desert Treasure I is considered an ice warrior for a Slayer assignment.

Ice warriors have good accuracy and can cut through Ranged and Magic armour with ease. They also seem to have higher levels of aggression than many other mobs as they'll often engage the player from a rather long distance. If using melee, wearing at least adamant or rune armour and using high quality food is advised.

Fire spells are extremely strong against ice warriors. Using fire bolt with chaos gauntlets is an economical option and gives you a max hit of 30. If you receive ice warriors as a Slayer task, using your best fire spell will most likely be the fastest way to complete the task.

In the Asgarnian Ice Dungeon, they can be safespotted by trapping an ice warrior on one side of a plus-shaped formation of rocks (not to be confused with the floor ice spikes) in the north-western area of their room.

At the White Wolf Mountain they can be safespotted south of the middle dungeon marker outside of the triple ladder enclosure, though there are level 25 and 38 wolves which will be aggressive unless the player's combat level exceeds double their level.

exampleSetups.label: Ranged
exampleSetups.notes:
The simplest method to use is to primarily use a ranged weapon such as the Toxic blowpipe. Completing the fight caves with Ranged isn't overly challenging and serves as a viable option for nearly all account types. It is recommended to consider maximising damage output and prayer bonus, with consideration for ranged defence and, to a lesser amount, slash defence.

- Pros
- This method is simple, provides reliable damage output and typically involves wearing armour with appropriate defence already.

- Cons
- Using blood spells to heal might require removing armour temporarily.

Inventory:

- 2-3 Bastion potions (4)
- 4-6 Saradomin brews (4)
- Fill rest of slots with super restores or prayer potions (4), but you should have at least 1 restore to counteract the brews' effects on a 1:3 ratio of restores to brews (i.e. 3 doses of brew requires 1 dose of restore to counteract the effect of brews)
- A rune pouch filled with runes to cast blood spells to kill and heal off of Tz-Keks
- A weapon to autocast blood spells

Notes:

- If you find you don't need to heal often, for example, if you are a higher-levelled Defence/Combat, consider the cheaper inventory of 4 Saradomin brews, 4 Super restores, 3 Ranging potions, and for the rest of your inventory, Prayer potions.
- This is only a recommended inventory setup and will always vary between each player.
- The higher your Defence level, the less you need protective gear like Karil's leathertop or leatherskirt.

exampleSetups.label: Melee
exampleSetups.notes:
Many melee weapons have a theoretically high damage output but can be more tedious to use due to the flinching typically required. This is a poor option for a first fire cape attempt.

- Pros
- Fight Cave is heavily sped up and can be as fast as approximately 25 minutes.
- The first 30 waves are generally faster than using Ranged.

- Cons
- If you're *not* using a halberd you'll be attacking from within Jad's melee range, and will have to use Protect from Melee as well.
- Rangers and magers in the Fight Caves can also melee you, so you may take additional damage, especially from the mager, if not flinching.

While fighting Jad, players must keep Protect from Melee on, switching to Protect from Missiles/Protect from Magic depending on what he is using, before immediately switching back to Protect from Melee between each of Jad's attacks. This is because, unlike his magic and ranged attacks, his melee attack does not give the player any time to react; the player's melee protection prayer must already be activated in the event that he uses this attack, in order to avoid taking damage.
This can be skipped completely by using the noxious halberd from out of Jad's melee range.

A strategy used when meleeing is to use thralls in order to speed up the encounter. Another strategy used is casting the Vengeance spell to recoil some damage back to the NPC.

Inventory:

- 3-4 Divine super combat potion (4)
- 7-9 Saradomin brew (4)
- 13-15 Super restore (4)
- 2 Stamina potion(4)
- rune…

exampleSetups.label: Early-game iron
exampleSetups.notes:
The fire cape is an important milestone for many iron players, but getting there can be a little difficult, given the lower availability of good gear. This is a setup that is within reach for early-game iron players with mid-level stats and gear. Iron players at this stage usually have tier-50 and tier-60 gear (or can obtain it fairly easily) and maybe a barrows piece or two.

Using this setup means that you will likely need to conserve as much prayer as you can, and your kills will be well in excess of 60 minutes long (usually closer to 90+ minutes). Due to this, it's recommended that you don't downgrade your gear too much. You can minimize prayer costs by familiarizing yourself with safespot mechanics and selecting a safespot-friendly rotation (rotations 5 and 6 are especially convenient).

Irons within boosting range of 74 Fletching and 72 Hunter should use the Hunters' sunlight crossbow with Sunlight antler bolts. The increase in attack speed and range more than compensates for the decrease in accuracy on all but TzTok-Jad himself.

Many iron players using this setup will have completed Desert Treasure I, but are unlikely to have a rune pouch or an easy supply of blood spell runes. If you do, however, have a rune pouch and an easy supply of blood spell runes, do bring them. Additionally, if you have good upgrades (e.g. DK rings, god d'hide) or space-saving items (e.g. bolt pouch), consider bringing them, too. Bolts for the Hunters' crossbows cannot be stored in the bolt…

exampleSetups.label: Ranged (Atlatl)
exampleSetups.notes:
The Eclipse atlatl is a viable weapon for tackling the fight caves, but its unique scaling with melee strength and range accuracy requires some additional considerations, but provides potential benefits.

- Pros
- Provides reliable damage output and scales well with gear with reasonable defensive bonuses.
- Melee strength armour boosts the effectiveness of melee special attack weapons, such as dragon or burning claws, Voidwaker, if not relying purely on the atlatl's own special attack.
- The eclipse moon armour's set effect provides additional damage over time.

- Cons
- Ranged potions and strength potions are needed for maximum damage output.
- Forgoing use of the toxic blowpipe primarily forfeits access to venom (which can be significant with lower levels) and requires an additional inventory slot if using for its healing special attack.
- The atlatl is both shorter range and two handed, which can mean more damage taken.
- The faster attack speed means more ammo will be consumed over the course of the fight caves compared to some slower weapons.
- Limited access to prayer bonus.

Inventory:

- 2-3 Super strength potions and Ranging potions (4)
- 6-8 Saradomin brews (4)
- Fill rest of slots with super restores or prayer potions (4), but you should have at least 1 restore to counteract the brews' effects on a 1:3 ratio of restores to brews (i.e. 3 doses of brew requires 1 dose of restore to counteract the effect of brews)
- Optionally, a weapon to autocast blood spells to…

strategy: TzTok-Jad (translated as Hard/Rock/Obsidian Fire Elemental), commonly called Jad for short, is a volcanic creature and the boss of the TzHaar Fight Cave minigame.

With a combat level of 702, TzTok-Jad has a max hit of 97 and can easily kill most players in one hit with any of its three attacks: a Melee attack with its bite (max hit of 97), a blast of Magic in the form of a fireball (max hit of 95), and a boulder falling from the ceiling as a Ranged attack (max hit of 97). To add to the challenge, players must fight through waves of monsters in the TzHaar Fight Cave in order to reach TzTok-Jad and must do so solo and without being able to restock on supplies from the previous waves.
TzTok-Jad is the boss monster of the TzHaar Fight Cave, and is encountered on Wave 63 (the final wave).

Once TzTok-Jad is reached, fighting and defeating him requires decent skill and reflexes. It is possible to engage TzTok-Jad using Melee, but as TzTok-Jad's melee attack has no warning animation, players must have Protect from Melee active when in melee distance, and switch to Protect from Missiles or Protect from Magic once the respective warning animation is identified. Note though that Jad can attack with melee every, as opposed to its normal attack speed. When at a distance, TzTok-Jad only uses Ranged and Magic attacks, which can hit the player from up to 15 tiles away. While Jad has no defence bonuses, it is recommended to kill Jad with ranged, as it avoids the melee attack completely, only leaving the magic and ranged attacks for Jad.

As with all other off-colored monsters in the Fight Caves, locating where the orange Ket-Zek spawned will indicate Jad's spawn point. Like the Tok-Xil, Jad has a very long attack range, and players not using drawn out clients can find themselves being attacked by Jad without seeing the combat style he uses and where he comes from.

Like Ket-Zek, Jad's attacks can deal extremely high damage, and is even capable of killing lower-leveled players in one hit if not protected against. Jad's melee and ranged attacks have a max hit of 97, while the magic attack has a max hit of 95.

- Melee: TzTok-Jad thrusts forward with a sharp bite. He only does this if the player is within melee distance. Unlike the Magic and Ranged attacks, the Melee attack is instant.
- Magic: TzTok-Jad rears up on his hind legs and dangles his forward legs for a few seconds before launching a fireball from his mouth at the player.
- Ranged: TzTok-Jad rears up on his…

strategy: Jellies can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 52 Slayer and level 57 combat by various medium-level Slayer masters. They are found in the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon. They are popular to kill similarly to hellhounds due to their high drop rate of hard clue scrolls. While fairly weak, jellies have an unusually high Defence level compared to other similar monsters around their level.
It is not recommended to kill normal jellies in most circumstances as they have a fairly poor drop table and are very far from a bank.
Two stronger variants of jellies can be found on Zeah; the Warped Jelly in the Catacombs of Kourend, and the Chilled jelly in the Ruins of Tapoyauik/Grimstone Dungeon.
summary: A 52 Slayer task known for hard clue scrolls. Jellies attack with magic-based melee that bypasses physical armour, so either pray Protect from Melee to negate all damage or wear high magic-defence armour like dragonhide. The wiki does not recommend killing regular jellies in the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon (poor drops, far from a bank); instead do warped jellies in the multicombat Catacombs of Kourend, ideally bursting or barraging them, or the Wilderness Slayer Cave for Krystilia tasks where nine jellies sit in a cannonable multicombat area below level 30 Wilderness.

strategy: Jungle horrors are horrors that live on the island of Mos Le'Harmless. Players must have completed Cabin Fever to gain access to the island. They can be assigned as a Slayer task by Chaeldar and Vannaka. They are a weaker relative of the cave horrors that live inside the caves on the island. A witchwood icon is NOT required to kill jungle horrors.
Players with under level 70 Defence are advised to bring food (lobsters or better) and armour to negate the jungle horror's relatively accurate melee attacks.

Alternatively, players with a high Defence level can sustain themselves by cutting jungle horrors' commonly dropped pineapples. Simply bring a knife to cut it into pineapple slices. This will heal 8 Hitpoints per pineapple. The NPC Joe right next to the gate sells stews and wine.

There is a single spawn near the opening in the northern Mos Le'Harmless wall which will not run away when damaged from behind the wall and can thus be easily safespotted. There is a set of spawns on the north-east corner of the wall which will not run away when using ranged or magic and can be safespotted. There are also many plants and trees which can be used to safespot several different jungle horror spawns slightly west of Mos Le'Harmless' northern gate.
summary: Jungle horrors are aggressive melee (stab) attackers on the island of Mos Le'Harmless, assigned by Vannaka and Chaeldar; no witchwood icon is needed, unlike cave horrors. Players under 70 Defence should bring good food and armour against their accurate melee, while higher-level players can sustain off the pineapples they drop with a knife. The biggest camp of 10-12 is directly north of the settlement's exit and several spawns can be safespotted from behind the northern wall or trees.

strategy: Kalphites can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 15 combat by all Slayer masters, with the exception of Mortimer and the Wilderness Slayer master Krystilia. Kalphites come in a wide variety of levels, which is why they are possible tasks from all Slayer masters. They can be found in the Kalphite Lair in the north-west Kharidian Desert, as well as in a Slayer task-exclusive area, the Kalphite Cave, just east of Shantay Pass.

Kalphites comes in four varieties: workers, soldiers, and guardians, as well as the boss monster the Kalphite Queen. With the exception of the Queen, all Kalphites use melee attacks. Additionally the soldiers and guardians can induce poison starting at 4 and 6 Hitpoints damage respectively. This poison bypasses protection prayers. Protect from Melee and some type of poison immunity will completely negate damage from the workers, soldiers and guardians.
summary: A common task from every master except Mortimer and Krystilia. All kalphites except the Queen use melee, and soldiers and guardians poison (starting at 4 and 6) through protection prayers, so Protect from Melee plus poison immunity negates everything. The wiki says tasks should be done in the task-only Kalphite Cave east of Shantay Pass, whose open multicombat chambers are cannonable and need no rope: cannon workers for a fast task or soldiers for XP, and avoid guardians. If Konar forces the Kalphite Lair, cannon the soldiers on the upper level; the Queen is not worth it without the Elite Desert Diary shortcut.

strategy: The Kalphite Queen (Kalphiscarabeinae pasha), also called the KQ, is the strongest of the Kalphites.

She is a powerful opponent that makes use of protection prayers, though they only function as an indicator to players of which attack styles may be most effective rather than outright blocking damage from them. She can use all three combat styles, of which her ranged and magic attacks always land as successful hits, and has two forms.

Unique drops from the Queen include the dragon 2h sword, dragon chainbody, dragon pickaxe and kq head drops. Killing her is additionally a requirement for the Desert Diary, with a hard task requiring players to kill her once and an elite task requiring the player to speak to a mounted head inside their own Player-owned house.

requiredItems: Insulated boots
strategy: Killerwatts are Slayer monsters located in the Killerwatt plane, accessible through a portal at the top floor of Draynor Manor after completion of Ernest the Chicken. A Slayer level of 37 is required to kill them.

If a player is not wearing a pair of insulated boots while fighting them, both their Ranged and Melee attacks will have a much higher maximum hit. Even when wearing insulated boots, their attacks are still rapid and highly accurate. A dwarf multicannon cannot be set up in the Killerwatt plane.
Killerwatts are a commonly skipped Slayer task due to their relatively high damage output combined with their mediocre drops, except for those seeking their unique air diamond drop.

While Killerwatts initially appear as passive floating orbs of electricity, they will immediately transform and move towards you when clicked on, rather than when attacked. They will switch between attacking with melee and ranged, depending on the player's distance from them and whether or not they are able to attack the player. For example, attacking a Killerwatt in melee range and then safespotting it will result in it switching to ranged attacks.

It is recommended to use either Ranged or Magic against them due to their negative ranged defences and weakness to air spells, as well as being able to easily restrict the Killerwatts to ranged attacks. Melee can be used as well if using a weapon such as a Halberd, as careful use of their extra range lets you lock the Killerwatts into using ranged attacks.
The Killerwatt's damage bonus from the player not wearing insulated boots does not hit through the correct protection prayer.
summary: A 37 Slayer task assigned only by Mazchna, done on the Killerwatt plane reached through Professor Oddenstein's portal at the top of Draynor Manor after Ernest the Chicken. Insulated boots are required: without them both their melee and ranged attacks hit up to 15 instead of 6 and 8, though the bonus does not go through the correct protection prayer. They appear as passive orbs but transform and rush you as soon as they are clicked, and switch between melee and ranged by distance, so Ranged or Magic (air spells) from a safespot locks them into ranged attacks.
usefulItems: Protect from Missiles or Melee as appropriate

exampleSetups.notes:
Using the passive damage bonus from the dragon hunter wand, it is possible to outheal the chip damage dealt by the boss and thus the only interaction needed is drinking potions every 5 minutes or so to maintain antifire protection and prayer. This is a very effective method for pet hunting due to the extremely long trip lengths and low interaction requirements, however can be costly due to the high cost of blood barrage. Due to the high cost of items used, it is strongly recommended to use the following method to move gear inside the KBD lair without risking being killed in the Wilderness:

- Enter KBD's lair with no armour equipped, and 4 low value items in inventory. Die to KBD to spawn a gravestone inside the lair.
- Withdraw all gear and potions required, and die a PvM death (e.g. to the Guard (Prifddinas) outside of the Prifddinas house portal with assistance from a locator orb). These items will be added to the gravestone within KBD's lair.
- Return to KBD's lair and withdraw all items from the gravestone.

- Notes
- It is not recommended to bank most loot from the boss using this method, as this will significantly reduce kills per hour.
- The best method to resupply is to die to the boss, and return to KBD's lair with only potions.

strategy: The King Black Dragon, commonly referred to as KBD, is a three-headed dragon located in his lair, accessible only through the deep Wilderness. With a combat level of 276, he is one of the strongest dragons in Old School RuneScape.

His lair is a multicombat area. Though designated as a Wilderness boss, the lair itself is not in the Wilderness, so players cannot attack each other and there are no teleport restrictions. Completion of the Wilderness Diary also does not note his bone drops.

Players can pay to fight the King Black Dragon in an instanced area inaccessible by other players (right-click Private option on lever). Players do not need to carry coins on them, as the fee may be deducted from the bank. Items dropped by the boss in this instance will disappear after 30 minutes, though items dropped by the player will disappear after the typical 3 minutes.

strategy: The Kraken is a stronger and larger version of the cave kraken. It requires level 87 Slayer to kill and cannot be boosted. Located at the Kraken Cove, it can only be attacked if the player has it, or cave krakens as a Slayer task, which also requires level 50 Magic. Alongside its non-boss variants, it is the only monster that drops the trident of the seas and Kraken tentacle.

Like its smaller brethren, the Kraken is submerged underwater. Magic is the only reliable way of damaging it, as Ranged deals 1/7th of its normal damage. The Kraken cannot be reached with Melee weapons, and is additionally entirely immune to melee attacks, displaying the message if you were to hit it with a melee weapon with long enough range to reach it. To start the fight, players can use a fishing explosive on the large whirlpool. Otherwise, the four whirlpools around must first be disturbed; when all four whirlpools are disturbed, the larger one can be disturbed, which will result in the Kraken waking up. Either method will release level 112 Enormous Tentacles.

Both the Kraken and Enormous Tentacles use typeless Magic, and as such Protect from Magic does not provide any degree of damage reduction. The Kraken can hit very hard, but has very poor accuracy, while the tentacles are much more accurate but deal less damage. The Kraken's projectile resembles Fire Wave.
summary: The Kraken is the 87 Slayer boss version of the cave kraken in Kraken Cove near the Piscatoris Fishing Colony; it can only be attacked while on a Kraken or cave kraken task, needs 50 Magic, must be fought with Magic, and can be instanced for 25,000 coins.

Tumeken's shadow is currently the only weapon capable of killing Kree'arra directly that is competitive with black chinchompas. Note that it is dramatically more effective than any other magic weapon in this encounter, dealing roughly three times as much damage as the next strongest option. As such, no other magic weapons are recommended for killing Kree'arra directly.

exampleSetups.label: Chinchompas
exampleSetups.notes:
By using chinchompas, one can kill Kree'arra quickly even if they are soloing, though it is also expensive.

To use this method, stand in the south-western corner of the room and wait for both Kree'arra and Flight Kilisa, the melee bodyguard, to close in on you.

When both are in position, start throwing chinchompas at Flight Kilisa; the chinchompas will almost always hit her due to her lower Defence, and the AoE damage will hit Kree'arra.

Players should stand under Kree'arra after each hit to minimise the amount of attacks Kree'arra can use against the player, especially if using a Twisted Bow as its attack speed is slower than Bow of Faerdhinen

exampleSetups.notes:
Even though Kree'arra has extremely high melee defences, the special attack of the soulflame horn can be used to make the player's next melee hit always land. Since the horn's special attack only works if another player is near the user, it is mandatory to kill Kree'arra in a small team with this method, with duos and trios working the best. Additionally, the player must be using a halberd since Kree'arra is airborne; the noxious halberd is the only viable halberd for this method.

All players should stand under Kree'arra after every attack, and use the soulflame horn's special attack while under him. While it is possible for a team to use only one soulflame horn and simply trade the horn between players after killing the minions, it is recommended for all players to have a soulflame horn in the event the player currently using the horn uses all of their special attacks (and thus guaranteed hits for the party) before Kree'arra is dead.

Despite melee armour giving high ranged defence bonuses, it is still recommended to pray Protect from Missiles to avoid potentially getting comboed by Kree'arra. Switch to Protect from Magic after Kree'arra dies to kill the magic minion.

strategy: Kurask are Slayer monsters that require a Slayer level of 70 to kill. Like turoth, they can only be damaged with leaf-bladed weapons, broad ammunition, or the Magic Dart spell due to their tough hides; they are immune to any other types of attacks. They are, however, susceptible to burn damage from weapons such as burning claws.

Kurask are relatively inaccurate, but they can hit somewhat high if their attacks manage to land. Additionally, they have fast health regeneration, healing one hitpoint every five game ticks. Due to their relative inaccuracy, they can be fought without protection prayers by using Bones to Peaches for healing, though players may wish to activate Protect from Melee if the superior version, the king kurask, spawns.

Although kurask are invulnerable to any damage from the special attacks of Saradomin godsword, ancient godsword, and toxic blowpipe, their healing effects will still activate as if damage had been dealt, making them useful as special attack weapons during extended trips. Likewise, the special attacks of ancient mace and eldritch Nightmare staff will restore prayer points based on what damage would have been dealt. The set effect of Guthan's equipment will not activate against kurask, however.
summary: Kurask require 70 Slayer and can only be damaged with leaf-bladed weapons, broad arrows or bolts, or Magic Dart; everything else (including cannons and thralls) deals no damage. They hit inaccurately with crush up to 11, so most players melee with a leaf-bladed battleaxe under Protect from Melee, or skip prayer and heal with Bones to Peaches. The Fremennik Slayer Dungeon (fairy ring AJR) has 5 kurask plus a 9-spawn task-only area; the Iorwerth Dungeon (Song of the Elves) has 14 tightly grouped kurask that also drop crystal shards. Bring an herb sack and alch runes since the task is profitable.

trainingSummary.cons: Can only be harmed with leaf-bladed weaponry, broad bolts or Magic Dart, which results in poor experience rates. Not worth doing for XP unless Slayer points are an issue.

requiredItems: Anti-dragon shield, dragonfire shield, dragonfire ward or ancient wyvern shield, and/or antifire potion
strategy: Lava dragons are former red dragons that have been transformed after being surrounded by lava for too long. They reside in the Lava Dragon Isle in the Wilderness (between level 36 and 42 Wilderness), and attack with melee as well as with dragonfire. Due to their low Magic level they are particularly weak to Magic, which combined with their weakness to water spells makes water bolt a slow but profitable method of killing them.

Lava dragons can be safespotted both inside and outside their isle. The many piles of skeletons and edges at the isle allow for players to safespot them inside. Alternatively, players can camp some of the southern spawns outside the isle. Having 74 Agility is recommended when killing them to use the stepping stones to escape the isle, as the area is frequented by player killers.

Bringing a pestle and mortar is optional to grind the scales into shards, in addition to High Level Alchemy runes to alch their common adamant and rune equipment drops. Although it is possible to stay at the isle indefinitely using this method, it is advisable to bank every 10–20 minutes as the isle is commonly targeted by player killers.

strategy: Lesser demons can be assigned by Krystilia, Chaeldar, and Vannaka. They are combat level 82, 87, and 94 and all have the same drop table, with the exception of the Wilderness Slayer Cave.
When not killing lesser demons as part of a Krystilia task, players have many spots to choose from to kill lesser demons.

The most common spots would be the Chasm of Fire and Catacombs of Kourend. The former can drop contracts after speaking to Yama after A Kingdom Divided, which makes killing the demons there much more lucrative compared to any other spot. However, catering to the preferred method will slow down times. There are four demons in a very small area, which allows for easy AFK times. The demons in the Catacombs are in a multicombat area and can be AFK'ed with access to the catacombs table, but a dwarf multicannon is not allowed. If none of these locations are available, it is best to kill them in the Crandor and Karamja Dungeon; the southern area contains six lesser demons with a fair amount of safespots and allows a cannon.

strategy: Lizardman can be assigned as a Slayer task after being unlocked at a cost of 75 Slayer reward points via the Reptile got ripped ability.

Normal lizardmen come in three forms; a plain level 53 and 62 variant, and the level 75 lizardman brute. These are simple enemies and have a weak poison that starts at 3 damage. They have very few lucrative drops, so these variants are primarily killed for the sake of speeding through a task with a cannon, often at the Lizardman Canyon due to it being a multicombat area.

The stronger shamans can be found in more sparse locations, and are more commonly killed as they drop the valuable dragon warhammer, which is popular for players who cannot acquire an elder maul. Lizardmen shamans require the use of Shayzien armour in order to kill them, as they have a unique poison spit that can deal up to 30 damage, which is fully blocked while wearing a full set of tier 5 shayzien armour. They also have various mechanics that make them harder to kill, though they are still easily dealt with using a ranged weapon and Protect from Missiles.
summary: Only assignable after buying 'Reptile got ripped' for 75 points from Chaeldar, Konar, Nieve or Duradel. Plain lizardmen and brutes are weak, poisonous (3) crush/ranged attackers with poor drops, so the task is usually blitzed with a cannon at the multicombat Lizardman Canyon east side (34 lizardmen plus 28 brutes). Players hunting the dragon warhammer kill lizardman shamans instead, ideally in the Lizardman Temple under Molch where the spawn explosions and jump AoE are smaller; shamans need Shayzien armour (tier 5 fully blocks the 25-30 acid spit) and Protect from Missiles at range. Killing lizardmen does not progress a normal Lizards task.

exampleSetups.label: Magic
exampleSetups.notes: Fire spells are especially powerful, causing both a damage-over-time effect and lowering the boss's magic defence. Generally, fire surge with a tome of fire and sunfire runes or searing pages will outperform the Tumeken's shadow. This is much more beneficial than thralls and Death Charge, as the only special attack needed is the Eye of Ayak to lower the boss's magic defence, which costs 50% energy and is easily restored over the course of a single kill. Apply the ayak special when the boss has 5 burn stacks.

exampleSetups.label: Ranged
exampleSetups.notes: Heavy ranged options, which require bolts, are the most effective ranged weapons to use on the Maggot King. While cheaper than magic, players will usually have longer kills and shorter trips as damage leading up to the melee phase is heavily reliant on enchanted ruby bolts, which forces the player to keep health low to avoid as much self-damage as possible. Additionally, a standard ranged weapon is required to deal with ur-maggots. Dizana's quiver allows bringing both ammo types without using extra switches or inventory slots but caution is advised if the player brings a melee cape switch, as failing to switch back to quiver can result in failing to fire. A charged bow such as a Bow of Faerdhinen, Crystal bow or Webweaver bow is a good way to get around this problem while also providing a nine to ten tile range to hit larvae. A venator bow is another option for killing larvae as the shots can bounce to the boss for extra damage, and also bounce to other larvae spawns to kill multiple in 1 click. It does have slightly less range than other bow options however so take care to not be dragged into hazards.

strategy: The Maggot King is a boss in Vampyrium that requires completion of The Blood Moon Rises to kill. The entrance to its lair can be found in the forest east of Sangvesti, near the Ruined Village.

Players may only fight the boss by themselves, and the fight takes place inside an instance. Additionally, a mix of melee and either magic or ranged is required to fight the Maggot King, as it cannot be attacked with melee until it falls below ~980 hitpoints (65%).

The Maggot King is the most mature and strongest form of the ur-maggot, a parasitic entity that kills its host and later possesses its body. This ur-maggot seems to have killed and then taken over the body of a powerful venator.
summary: The Maggot King is a solo, instanced boss in Vampyrium (east of Sangvesti near the Ruined Village) that requires The Blood Moon Rises and 74 Slayer, assigned as a boss task by Konar, Nieve and Duradel.

strategy: Magic axes are monsters that resemble translucent iron battleaxes.
The axes in the magic axe hut can be given as a wilderness Slayer assignment by Krystilia. Players require 23 Thieving for magic axes to be assigned as a task.
summary: A Krystilia-only task at the Magic Axe Hut in level 54 Wilderness, which needs 23 Thieving and a lockpick to open either door. The hut is full of aggressive level 42 magic axes that slash for up to 5; it is single-way combat but a cannon can be placed inside. Get there via the Ardougne or Edgeville lever to the Deserted Keep, run north, slash the web and go east, or take a Wilderness Obelisk to level 50 and run west past the Rogues' Castle and Chaos Elemental. It is above level 30 Wilderness, so no teleports work from the hut.

strategy: Mammoths are a species of elephant-like creatures that inhabit the area south-east of the Ferox Enclave. They are not very intelligent.

Mammoths can be easily safespotted due to their large size (3x3). Players can use the many trees or tree stumps in the area to safespot them from behind. It is an efficient place to train with a Dwarf multicannon due to the high hitpoints of the Mammoths, a nearby altar providing unlimited Prayer for boosts, and the short walk to the Enclave for resupplying. However, players are vulnerable to player killers while training and are therefore advised not to carry too many supplies on them at once.
Killing a Mammoth is a task in the Easy Wilderness Diary.
summary: A Krystilia-only task in low Wilderness (level 7-14) south-east of Ferox Enclave, west of the Chaos Temple. Mammoths are big 3x3 stab attackers with only a 7 max hit and lots of hitpoints, so they are trivially safespotted behind the trees and stumps and are an excellent cannon target; the nearby altar restores prayer and Ferox Enclave is a short walk for resupply.
usefulItems: Ranged or magic gear for tree safespots

exampleSetups.label: Melee
exampleSetups.notes:
Melee is an efficient way of killing them, especially with a Dragon hunter lance (the best stab weapon against Dragons and draconic creatures) and using Sunfire armour for Prayer or high-tier armour, such as Bandos or Barrows equipment, for Defence. The Dragon hunter lance is the best choice followed by Osmumten's fang. Other options include Ghrazi rapier, Zamorakian hasta and lastly Abyssal Dagger. Using slash weapons, such as an Abyssal whip, is not recommended due to their high slash defences. As their Defence is extremely high, the higher the stab bonus the faster the kills will be, thus using fewer supplies.

Inventory:

- Holy wrench (optional)
- 2-3 Extended super antifires potions
- 1-2 Super combat potions
- 30+ Nature runes and 150+ Fire runes for Alchs (optional)
- Food is not necessary when fighting bronze, iron or steel dragons with protect from melee.

exampleSetups.label: Ranged
exampleSetups.notes:
Ranged can be feasible and very economical if using broad bolts, but using Diamond bolts (e) can be faster at a greater cost. Always keep a distance of several spaces away from the dragon to avoid its melee attack. All you have to do is make sure your antifire is active, and snipe away at a distance.

Inventory:

- 1 Extended super antifire
- 1-2 Prayer potions (optional) Unlike melee, Prayer potions are really not needed when using range unless Eagle Eye or Rigour is used
- 1-2 Ranging potions
- 30+ Nature runes and 150+ Fire runes for Alchs (optional)
- Food is not necessary when fighting bronze, iron or steel dragons from a distance.

exampleSetups.label: Magic
exampleSetups.notes:
Magic is one of the quickest ways to kill metal dragons cheaply, and can be done without taking damage. All the caster has to do is make sure their antifire is active, anti-dragon shield is equipped and attack them at a distance. Unless using a powered staff, earth spells should be used to take advantage of the dragons' earth weakness.
Although players can opt for better setups if maging, Void mage can be used as well for accounts below 70 Defence. However, Ahrim's robes will prove to be better when players have level 70 Defence or higher.

Inventory:

- 1 Extended super antifire
- 1-2 Prayer potions (optional) Unlike Melee, Prayer potions are really not needed when using Magic unless Mystic Might or Augury is used
- Nature and Fire runes for Alchs (optional)
- Food is not necessary when fighting bronze, iron or steel dragons from a distance.

exampleSetups.label: Mithril dragon: Melee
exampleSetups.notes:
Melee is a very effective method of killing mithril dragons with little upkeep cost, assuming that the player has high combat stats (at least 90+), and access to either the Osmumten's fang or a dragon hunter lance. If the player does not have either the fang or lance, ghrazi rapier and zamorakian hasta are still viable options, however Magic then usually becomes more effective, depending on the player's equipment. For the best damage output, it is strongly recommended to use a defender and use extended super antifire potions to negate the dragonfire damage, instead of an anti-dragon shield or dragonfire shield.

This specific setup focuses on an offensive approach, resulting in higher kills per hour, at the cost of requiring more attention and supplies than a tank-based method.

When meleeing, players take damage from two combat styles and will have to tank both in order to survive. It is best to wear Torva or Bandos armour for their strength bonus and good defensive bonuses, and use Protect from Magic. Players can also wear Eclipse moon chestplate and Blood moon tassets for a minimal loss of max hit, in exchange for gaining much higher Magic defence. If the player does not have Torva or Bandos armour, wearing armour with high Magic defence (such as Karil's armour or black dragonhide armour) and using Protect from Melee will suffice. Piety should also be used in conjunction with the chosen protection prayer for better damage output and higher Defence.

Inventory:

- A games…

exampleSetups.label: Mithril dragon: Magic
exampleSetups.notes:
Magic is one of the most effective ways to kill mithril dragons with high-level equipment. With best-in-slot gear available, Tumeken's shadow offers the highest damage output off-task and second-highest on-task. Using the harmonised Nightmare staff and casting Earth Surge also offers good DPS due to the dragon's 50% elemental weakness to earth spells. Lesser powered staves, such as the sanguinesti staff or trident of the swamp are solid options as well, particularly at high Magic levels due to the way their damage scales with level. At lower Magic levels, it may be better to use strong earth spells to take advantage of the elemental weakness. Compared to Magic, using Melee is much more cost-effective, and the dragon hunter lance offers comparable or higher damage output in most cases.

Players should wear equipment that maximises Magic damage and accuracy bonuses. When maging, players should stand at a distance and use Protect from Missiles. Lastly, Augury, Mystic Vigour, or Mystic Might should be used for better damage output and higher Magic defence.

If the player is not wearing an ancient wyvern shield or an anti-dragon shield, players must use super antifire potions (or their extended versions) to negate the dragonfire damage.

Inventory:

- A games necklace
- A rune pouch
- A teleport
- Imbued heart or magic potion(s) (optional)
- 1-2 antifires
- 4-5 prayer potions
- High-healing food for the rest

exampleSetups.label: Mithril dragon: Ranged
exampleSetups.notes:
Ranged is a similar option to Magic in that damage taken will be largely prevented by Protect from Missiles and high magic defence bonuses from equipment. Due to the high ranged defence of Mithril dragons, the high Ranged Attack bonus granted against dragons by the dragon hunter crossbow is all but necessary. It is still possible to kill mithril dragons with other crossbows, but Melee and Magic set-ups will outperform the Ranged style with ease. Ruby dragon bolts (e) and diamond dragon bolts (e) are very effective, but come at a high cost and can only be used if using a Dragon crossbow or better. If using enchanted ruby dragon bolts, players should switch to their enchanted diamond dragon bolts at 100-150 HP. Amethyst broad bolts can be used instead as a more cost-effective ammunition alternative, but can significantly increase the time taken for a kill.

Players should use Protect from Missiles with Rigour or Eagle Eye. Since Ranged armour has high Magic defence, all magic damage should be tanked but Rigour will be a large boost as unlike Eagle Eye it provides some defensive bonuses of its own.

Inventory:

- A games necklace
- A teleport
- 1-2 divine ranging potions
- 1-2 antifires
- 4-5 prayer potions
- High-healing food for the rest

exampleSetups.label: Mithril dragon: Melee tank
exampleSetups.notes:
While offensive armour is generally better for a high amount of kills per hour, focussing on defensive gear will allow the player to kill mithril dragons with relatively low effort and for extended amounts of kills per trip, making it a viable choice for those intending to grind out many hundreds or thousands of mithril dragons in their hunt for a dragon full helm or draconic visage.

The Osmumten's fang or dragon hunter lance are still the best choice for the weapon, but instead of offensive armour, Justiciar armour (only when wearing the full set) in combination with an elysian spirit shield can be used to effectively block out 15% + 17.5% of all incoming damage. Combined with optional recoil effects from the ring of suffering and echo boots, as well as the healing effect of the amulet of blood fury will make for an incredibly tanky setup that will allow for trips that are only terminated when the player runs out of antifire potions or prayer potions.

Using protect from Magic and piety as well as stat boosting potions will greatly help. When no or few specialized tanking equipment is owned by the player, they should consider focussing on offensive stats as listed in the 'Melee' style equipment tab instead. Where viable tanking options are lacking, the player might prefer to instead use offensive gear in that slot. Especially when justiciar armour or an elysian spirit shield is already used, it is still very viable to use a tank setup with more offensive hand, feet and…

exampleSetups.label: Adamant dragon: Melee
exampleSetups.notes:
With base 90 Melee stats and a Ghrazi rapier, dragon hunter lance, or an Osmumten's fang using melee against adamant dragons is a reliable option. With worse weapons, magic or ranged may be more effective. Adamant dragons have accurate and strong attacks, so Bandos, Justiciar or Barrows equipment is recommended along with Protect from Magic and Piety in tandem to reduce damage taken. Also, Vengeance can be used for dealing with their Blood Forfeit Ranged attacks. A dwarf multicannon may also be used here with significant accuracy.

Inventory:

- Digsite pendant or a mounted one in POH with house tabs
- Special attack weapon choice
- 1 divine super combat potion, super combat potion or super set
- 1 extended antifire, or extended super antifire if using a shield without dragonfire protection
- 3-4 prayer potions
- 1-2 antidote++, antidote+, superantipoison or antipoison if not using a serpentine helm
- Rune pouch with runes to cast Vengeance or High Level Alchemy (set warning value to 162,000) (optional)
- One-click teleport (optional)
- Food (sharks / manta rays / anglerfish / karambwan)
- Bracelet of slaughter (optional, if on task)
- Dwarf multicannon
- steel cannonball (optional, about 400 used per hour)

exampleSetups.label: Adamant dragon: Ranged
exampleSetups.notes:
With level 90 Ranged and a dragon hunter crossbow (DHCB), adamant dragons can easily be killed due to the crossbow's passive effect, as well as circumventing their melee attack. A Twisted Bow provides comparable damage to a DHCB if not slightly more depending on luck. Armadyl or Karil's equipment is recommended along with Protect from Missiles and Rigour or Eagle Eye in tandem. Also, Vengeance could be used for dealing with their Blood Forfeit Ranged attacks. A dwarf multicannon may be used here with significant accuracy.

Inventory:

- Digsite pendant or a mounted one in POH with house tabs
- 1 divine ranging potion or ranging potion
- 1 extended antifire, or extended super antifire if using a shield without dragonfire protection
- 3-4 prayer potions
- 1-2 antidote++, antidote+, superantipoison or antipoison if not using a serpentine helm
- Rune pouch with runes to cast Vengeance or High Level Alchemy (set warning value to 162,000) (optional)
- One-click teleport (optional)
- Food (sharks / manta rays / anglerfish / karambwan)
- Bracelet of slaughter (optional, if on task)
- dwarf multicannon (optional)
- steel cannonball (optional, about 400 cannonballs used per hour)

exampleSetups.label: Adamant dragon: Magic - Tumeken's Shadow
exampleSetups.notes:
Tumeken's shadow's high accuracy and damage from its passive effect makes it one of the fastest options for killing adamant dragons, provided the player has enough damage-boosting magic equipment such as an occult necklace and ancestral robes. If not on a slayer task, this makes it even faster than using dragonbane weaponry.

Inventory:

To maximize inventory space for food to increase trip length, you should pre-pot a dose of antidote++ and an anglerfish, and use a max cape, Construction cape, or house tabs to teleport to your POH to use your mounted digsite pendant. When fighting, stay out of melee distance and use Protect from Missiles and (optional) Augury. If not using Augury, fewer prayer potions are needed.

- Saturated heart
- Extended super antifire(2)
- 4 prayer potions
- Divine rune pouch with runes for Vengeance
- High healing food (manta rays / anglerfish / tuna potatoes / sea turtles / sharks / karambwan)
- Max cape for teleport to house and bank. Can be replaced with Construction cape or house tabs for a one-click teleport to house only
- Bracelet of slaughter (optional, if on task)

exampleSetups.label: Adamant dragon: Magic
exampleSetups.notes:
While not as effective as using Tumeken's shadow, due to adamant dragons' elemental weakness and relatively low Magic defence, Earth spells can be a viable alternative, especially when used with a dragon hunter wand and/or while on a slayer task.

Inventory:

- Digsite pendant or a mounted one in POH with house tabs
- Saturated heart / imbued heart
- 1 extended antifire, or extended super antifire if using a shield without dragonfire protection
- 3-4 prayer potions
- 1-2 antidote++, antidote+, superantipoison or antipoison if not using a serpentine helm
- Rune pouch with runes to cast the spell of choice
- One-click teleport (optional)
- Food (sharks / manta rays / anglerfish / karambwan)
- Bracelet of slaughter (optional, if on task)

exampleSetups.label: Rune dragon: Melee
exampleSetups.notes:
With base 90 Melee stats and Osmumten's fang or dragon hunter lance, using melee against rune dragons is a reliable option. With worse weapons, magic or ranged may be more effective. Rune dragons have accurate and strong attacks, so Bandos, Justiciar, or Barrows equipment is recommended along with Protect from Magic and Piety in tandem to reduce damage taken. Vengeance can be used against their healing Ranged attacks. As soon as a number appears in a purple hitsplat on the dragon, cast Vengeance.

Additionally, you may bring Thralls along with a Book of the Dead. Thralls deal 1-3 damage every couple of seconds so this adds up significantly.

A Dwarf multicannon may also be used against rune dragons with a significant level of accuracy.

- Inventory

- Digsite pendant or a mounted one in POH with house tabs
- Special attack weapon choice
- 1 divine super combat potion, super combat potion or super set
- 1 extended antifire, or extended super antifire if using a shield without dragonfire protection
- 3-4 prayer potions
- Rune pouch with runes to cast Vengeance or High Level Alchemy (set warning value to 162,000) (optional)
- One-click teleport (optional)
- Food (sharks / manta rays / anglerfish / karambwan)
- Bracelet of slaughter (optional, if on task)
- Dwarf multicannon (optional)
- Steel cannonball (about 400 per hour)

exampleSetups.label: Rune dragon: Ranged
exampleSetups.notes:
With level 90 Ranged and a dragon hunter crossbow, rune dragons can easily be killed due to the crossbow's passive effect, as well as circumventing their melee attack. Protect from Missiles is recommended with Rigour or Eagle Eye in tandem. Also, Vengeance could be used for dealing with their healing Ranged attacks, which hits through Protect from Missiles. As soon as a number appears in a purple hitsplat on the dragon, prepare Vengeance. Additionally, you may bring Thralls along with a Book of the Dead. Thralls deal 1-3 damage every couple of seconds so this adds up significantly. A dwarf multicannon may also be used with good accuracy due to ranged gear's high bonuses.

- Inventory

- Digsite pendant or a mounted one in POH with house tabs
- 1 divine ranging potion or ranging potion
- 1 extended antifire, or extended super antifire if using a shield without dragonfire protection
- 3-4 prayer potions
- Rune pouch with runes to cast Vengeance or High Level Alchemy (set warning value to 162,000) (optional)
- One-click teleport (optional)
- Food (sharks / manta rays / anglerfish / karambwan)
- Bracelet of slaughter (optional, if on task)
- Dwarf multicannon (optional)
- Steel cannonball (optional, about 400 per hour)

exampleSetups.label: Rune dragon: Magic
exampleSetups.notes:
Rune dragons have relatively low Magic defence. The most effective weapon for killing rune dragons across all styles is the Tumeken's shadow, surpassing even dragonbane weaponry.

For those without a Shadow, Earth spells can be a viable alternative, especially when used with a dragon hunter wand and/or while on a slayer task. Protect from Missiles is recommended due to the dragons' accurate ranged attacks.

- Inventory

- Digsite pendant or a mounted one in POH with house tabs
- Saturated heart
- 1 extended antifire, or extended super antifire if using a shield without dragonfire protection
- 3-4 prayer potions
- Rune pouch with runes to cast the spell of choice
- One-click teleport (optional)
- Food (sharks / manta rays / anglerfish / karambwan)
- Bracelet of slaughter (optional, if on task)

strategy: Metal dragons can be assigned by high-levelled slayer masters as a potential task.
Players have many options for killing these dragons:

- Bronze dragons - found in Brimhaven Dungeon and the Catacombs of Kourend. The lowest level option.
- Iron dragons - found in the same locations as bronze dragons. More plentiful. Can also be found in the Isle of Souls dungeon.
- Steel dragons - found in Brimhaven Dungeon and the Catacombs of Kourend.
- Mithril dragons - found in the Ancient Cavern, requiring completion of the first part of the Firemaking section of the Barbarian Training miniquest.
- Adamant dragons - found in Lithkren Vault, requiring completion of Dragon Slayer II in order to access.
- Rune dragons - same as above.

summary: An 85 combat task from Konar, Nieve or Duradel that needs Dragon Slayer I started. All metal dragons breathe long-range dragonfire that Protect from Magic does not reduce, so full protection needs an antifire potion plus an anti-dragon or dragonfire shield, or a super antifire; they are draconic (dragon hunter lance/crossbow) and weakest to stab and earth spells. The quickest task is bronze dragons in the Brimhaven Dungeon task-only area (5 in a small cannonable room), or iron dragons if you want a visage chance; rune dragons at Lithkren Vault (Dragon Slayer II) are the profitable choice. Only mithril dragons (Ancient Cavern) cannot be cannoned.

Minotaurs are a common method of Ranged training as they can be safespotted and commonly drop iron arrows.

Minotaurs (level 12 and 27) are non-aggressive crush attackers with very low Defence, so any style works; the level has ranging safespots and is the only multicombat floor of the stronghold, and a cannon can be placed. They drop the right skull half for the skull sceptre and plenty of iron arrows.
